newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-BOOKIES PREDICT MORE GRAND NATIONAL BETS.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-BOOKIES PREDICT MORE GRAND NATIONAL BETS.

text.p: Britain's betting shops are expecting even more punters to bet on the Grand National on Monday after the race was postponed for 48 hours by a bomb alert on Saturday.
"Last year the industry turned over about 60 million pounds ($98 million) but this time it could reach 85 million," said Malcolm Palmer, public relations manager at bookmakers Coral.
"There are not many cancelling and there are opportunities now for a lot more to put a bet on today," said Palmer.
The industry had predicted wagers of 70 million pounds but this should easily be exceeded by the time the race is run at 1600 GMT, he said.
"There is no great indication of people wanting to cancel their bets," said Graham Sharpe, media relations manager at William Hill.
The Grand National is the single most important date in the betting calendar for the industry, which obtains about 10 percent of its total annual income from the race.

"It does give plenty of people another bite at the cherry. So I think we will see a few more bets being placed today," said Ed Nicholson, public relations manager at Ladbroke Group, Britain's largest chain of betting outlets.
The bookmakers are hoping that a rank outsider wins, unlike last year, when favourite Rough Quest took the honours at odds of 7-1.

Ladbrokes, which has taken a single 20,000s pound bet on Wylde Hide each way at 16-1, stands to lose some 500,000 pounds if the horse wins. The firm is also holding another 10,000 pounds stake to win on the same horse.
